builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Train What You Run: Probabilistic Convolutions for Learning Token Compaction in State Space Models
summary: ProbConv replaces heuristic or post-hoc token pruning in Mamba-style state space backbones by computing the exact expected convolution under independent keep probabilities, making token keep decisions differentiable during training. The cost is a modified training procedure with a custom operator and the need to retrain the target backbone rather than applying the method to a frozen or API-served model; inference itself uses the standard compacted block with binary decisions. It can fail when the reader cannot retrain the model, when backbones lack local convolutions (standard transformers are out of scope), or when compaction is light, since the reported advantage concentrates under strong token removal.
rationale: The method targets token compaction in convolution/SSM-based vision models and requires retraining with a custom differentiable operator, so it is only worth small-scale validation if the reader runs or fine-tunes Mamba-style backbones rather than calling third-party APIs.
technique: Differentiable token compaction for SSM convolutions

claims.statement: ProbConv replaces heuristic or post-hoc token pruning in Mamba-style state space backbones by computing the exact expected convolution under independent keep probabilities, making token keep decisions differentiable during training. The cost is a modified training procedure with a custom operator and the need to retrain the target backbone rather than applying the method to a frozen or API-served model; inference itself uses the standard compacted block with binary decisions. It can fail when the reader cannot retrain the model, when backbones lack local convolutions (standard transformers are out of scope), or when compaction is light, since the reported advantage concentrates under strong token removal.

ProbConv's accuracy advantage over matched training controls grows as more tokens are removed; in the Cobra vision-language model it outperforms adapted published pruning methods at matched inference budgets, and it improves over zero-mask training in video frame selection and speech frame dropping.
